subject: Request: temporary p95 stability relief + evidence delivery plan for Hosted API
messages:
From: Samantha Li <s.li@orchardhealth.ai>
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary p95 relief request during migration

Hi Connor,

Quick note from Orchard — we’re kicking off a user-data migration this weekend to move routing and prompt enrichment into our VPC layer. Our prep runs show transient tokenization/latency spikes that would push p95 above our contracted target for a handful of hours each day over the next two weeks.

We want to avoid repeated SLA exceptions while we complete the cutover. Can Redwood provide either: 1) a short, time‑boxed temporary relaxation of the hosted API p95 commitment, or 2) an operational carveout (measurement window change or maintenance carveout) for the migration window?

We can provide telemetry (sample traces and request metadata) and a short evidence bundle if that helps you evaluate. We’d prefer an approach that avoids credits if possible (we expect a short-lived event).

Key details:
- Impact window: 2026-05-29 02:00–10:00 UTC (expected daily spikes during retries)
- Estimated affected traffic: ~8% of requests, peak ~13% during bulk moves
- Current contract: p50 = 90ms, p95 = 480ms (5-minute measurement window)

Can you confirm next steps and what evidence Redwood would need to consider a temporary operational relief?

Best,
Samantha Li
Head of Platform Operations
Orchard Health
[Attachment: orchard_slo_evidence.zip (zip, 2.1MB) — sample traces + request metadata]

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Li <s.li@orchardhealth.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary p95 relief request during migration

Samantha — thanks for the heads up and the attachment. Appreciate the context.

Short answer: yes, we can evaluate a short, limited operational carveout instead of issuing credits. To move quickly, we need a clear, auditable plan and an evidence package that maps to the measurement windows we use for hosted SLOs.

What I propose (staged):
1) Immediate triage (this weekend): accept the evidence bundle and confirm there are no systemic regressions (we’ll run a quick sample check).
2) Provisional carveout: a temporary p95 relief window tied to your migration maintenance window for up to 14 days (we can agree on daily windows), with strict start/end times and an agreed list of request IDs to exclude if you can surface them.
3) Audit + backfill: you provide the telemetry sample (full traces + headers) and we’ll do a 48‑hour backfill analysis; if the analysis shows the impact is larger than stated, we’ll convert to credit pathways per contract.

Operational details we need from you to evaluate and implement the carveout:
- Exact timezone-normalized windows (ISO timestamps) for each migration day
- Example request IDs or a small sampling filter (e.g., path=/api/v1/gen and header X-Mig-Run: orchard-2026-05-29)
- The telemetry bundle (your zip looks like it contains traces; we’ll need 200–500 sample traces and at least one day of aggregated histograms)

Marissa and Ben — I’m looping you in to confirm whether the 14‑day provisional carveout and audit plan works from a commercial and SLA governance perspective. If yes, we’ll draft a short addendum (2–3 bullets) and log the carveout in the contract system.

Samantha — if you can confirm the daily windows and upload the full evidence link, I’ll schedule a quick internal review first thing tomorrow.

Thanks,
Connor O’Brien
Account Executive, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stub: [orchard_slo_evidence.zip (2.1MB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, Samantha Li <s.li@orchardhealth.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary p95 relief request during migration

Thanks Connor — and hi Samantha. Logged this with Contracts & Ops. Quick operational proposal from our side so you have concrete terms to review: 

Proposed carveout terms (summary):
- Scope: Hosted API p95 commitment only (p50 unchanged)
- Temporal window: daily carveout 02:00–10:00 UTC, effective 2026-05-29 through 2026-06-11 (14 days).
- Measurement change during carveout: we will exclude request IDs tagged by your migration header (or an agreed sampling filter) from p95 aggregation. Measurement window remains 5 minutes for non-exempt traffic; exempted traffic will be documented and excluded from SLA calculations.
- Evidence and audit: Redwood will run a backfill analysis after the carveout using the supplied traces and aggregated histograms. If aggregate impact exceeds 15% additional load (beyond your estimate) we will: (a) escalate to commercial for credits, and (b) propose a shortened carveout interval.
- Credit fallback: Credits will be calculated per contract appendix A; we will only pursue credits after mutual review of telemetry.
- Termination: Either party can terminate the carveout with 48 hours’ notice if we detect abuse or unreported scope expansion.

Operational checklist (what we need from Orchard, ideally by 2026-05-29 18:00 UTC):
- 200–500 sample traces + request-level metadata (already attached — thanks)
- A sampling filter or list of 5k request IDs (response-sample.csv attached)
- Confirmation of daily windows in ISO (we will hard-code in the measurement engine)
- List of endpoints to exclude (if different from /api/v1/gen)

Attachments included: [response-sample.csv (CSV, 42KB)], [credit-calc.xlsx (xlsx, 18KB)]

Next steps: If Orchard confirms, Contracts will generate a short addendum (one paragraph) and Operations will stage the exclusion rule in our measurement pipeline. We aim to have the exclusion active before your migration kickoff.

Marissa Cole
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
--
Attachment stubs: [response-sample.csv], [credit-calc.xlsx]

From: Samantha Li <s.li@orchardhealth.ai>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 29 May 2026 11:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Temporary p95 relief request during migration

Marissa / Connor — thanks, this looks good and pragmatic. We accept the provisional carveout terms as written. A couple of quick clarifications before you draft the addendum:

1) Regional failover: our migration will route ~30% of migrated traffic to eu-west-1 for validation. Are regional failovers handled automatically by the exclusion rule if the request header is present? We need cross-region behaviour to be consistent.
2) Audit logs: we need a time-limited CT-archive of the excluded request IDs and the final backfill report for our compliance team (SOC2 audit in Q3). Can Redwood provide a read-only Drive link to the backfill report and a signed receipt of exclusion list?

I’ve attached Orchard’s audit checklist for reference. Happy to sign the one‑paragraph addendum once Contracts shares it — please include the regional failover language if possible.

Thanks again,
Samantha
Head of Platform Operations
Orchard Health
[Attachment: orchard_audit_requirements.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]
